title: South Korea's power utility KEPCO confirms a breach that exposed data on 1.52 million people, including bank and card numbers
tldr: Korea Electric Power Corporation says an intruder took personal data on about 1.52 million customers, suppliers and staff from its billing platform and procurement system; the privacy regulator has opened an investigation.
byline: Seoul Economic Daily, Seoul Economic Daily (regulator probe), BleepingComputer

title: Nvidia's board reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive less than two weeks after his resignation
tldr: Nvidia's board voted unanimously to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO and president, saying input from senior US government officials convinced it that his return poses no national security risk.

title: Amazon buys Decart's chip-optimization software and hires its founders as it prepares to sell Trainium chips to customers
tldr: Amazon is acquiring the Decart Optimization Stack, software that tunes AI workloads for specific chips, along with Decart's founders and engineers, in a deal Bloomberg values at about $7.5 billion.

title: German media report that Russia could launch a nuclear-armed anti-satellite weapon into orbit as early as December
tldr: NDR, WDR and Süddeutsche Zeitung report that Western intelligence agencies believe Russia is preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite, which would threaten thousands of spacecraft in low Earth orbit; the Kremlin dismisses the claim.

title: Interrupt-Aware Static Detection of Deadlocks in Rust Operating Systems
tldr: A static analysis that tracks both held locks and interrupt state in Rust kernels, paired with an AI agent that audits its reports, found nine maintainer-confirmed deadlock bugs in four Rust operating systems.
byline: Yuzhi Li, Hongliang Tian, Chengjun Chen et al. · Fudan University; Ant Group

title: The FBI investigates an apparent breach of NCIC, the database police across the US use to check warrants and stolen property
tldr: CNN and the Associated Press report that the FBI is investigating an apparent intrusion into the National Crime Information Center; the bureau has not confirmed it and the scope is unknown.

title: Microsoft says attackers exploited an Entra Connect Health flaw to read administrator email addresses and tenant details
tldr: A flaw in Microsoft's Entra Connect Health API, present from July 23 until a fix on November 19, let outsiders read administrator contacts and tenant metadata; passwords and tokens were not exposed.

title: The FCC overrides California's landline rules, clearing AT&T to drop copper phone service for about 184,000 homes
tldr: The FCC ordered California to stop enforcing its Carrier of Last Resort rules against AT&T, which wants to end basic copper phone service for 184,000 residential and 15,000 business customers in June 2027.

title: F5 issues emergency hotfixes for critical BIG-IP flaws that can crash traffic handling and may allow remote code execution
tldr: F5 released out-of-band hotfixes for critical, unauthenticated BIG-IP flaws that can crash its traffic engine and may allow remote code execution; no mitigations exist besides patching.
byline: BleepingComputer, Canadian Centre for Cyber Security

title: Amazon says suspected Chinese hackers used the AI agent framework Cairn to find and exploit a zero-day at East Asian universities
tldr: Amazon found an exposed Cairn server showing AI agents that worked for hours without human direction, then discovered and used an unknown flaw in a medical imaging app to take over university servers.

title: UK surveillance tribunal confirms the Home Office served Apple a secret order over encrypted iCloud data
tldr: The Investigatory Powers Tribunal rejected the Home Office's secrecy argument and confirmed it served Apple a Technical Capability Notice, though the order's content stays secret ahead of a 2027 hearing.
byline: Investigatory Powers Tribunal judgment, The Register

title: Signal blocks screenshots by default to keep Siri and Gemini agents from reading private chats
tldr: Signal's iOS and Android apps now block screenshots by default so built-in AI agents cannot capture chats, and the company says operating systems give developers no robust way to stop such access.

title: Polymorph: Operating System Kernel Optimization Through Artificial Intelligence
tldr: Polymorph has an AI agent write one tunable Linux kernel policy, then tunes it live without a language model, beating Linux's defaults for page caching and scheduling at far lower cost than offline search.
byline: Dean Sysman, Georgios Liargkovas, Tal Zussman et al.

title: Chase, Visa and Mastercard confirm breaches at outside vendors after an extortion gang leaks customer data
tldr: JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard say vendors were breached, exposing customer names and email addresses but no card numbers, after the N0n extortion group posted their data online.

title: Broadcom patches a vCenter flaw that suspected Chinese state hackers exploited since September
tldr: Broadcom issued an emergency fix for a 9.8-rated vCenter Server authentication bypass that Mandiant says a suspected Chinese espionage group used as a zero-day to take over virtualized environments.

title: The European Commission confirms a cyberattack in which hackers used a public AI hacking tool
tldr: The European Commission says attackers using a publicly available AI tool disrupted staff payroll, leave and medical reimbursement systems for more than ten days, with no evidence so far of a broad data breach.

title: Congress publishes Nvidia and AMD's China chip licences, showing 879,000 AI chips approved
tldr: House committee chair Brian Mast released licence records showing US regulators approved more than 879,000 of 3.4 million requested Nvidia and AMD AI chips for China, including sales to Alibaba and Tencent.
byline: House Foreign Affairs Committee, The Register

title: YUL: Bringing Software Supply Chain Security to Coding Agents
tldr: YUL checks every software dependency a coding agent declares against the package registry and blocks stale or nonexistent versions, so agents end on the latest release in over 90% of affected runs.
byline: Aman Sharma, Frank Reyes, Martin Monperrus · KTH Royal Institute of Technology

title: Attackers publish two credential-stealing versions of Microsoft's official Agent Framework package on PyPI
tldr: Two malicious releases of Microsoft's agent-framework Python package, downloaded about 200,000 times a month, stole cloud and developer credentials; developers who installed versions 1.26.1 or 1.26.2 should rebuild and rotate secrets.

title: Intel signs its first outside customer for its 18A chip-making process, and Microsoft adopts its EMIB packaging
tldr: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan says an unnamed company has signed on to make chips with Intel's 18A-P process, and that 18A yields have reached 70%, a step for Intel's effort to compete with TSMC.

title: Microsoft previews Windows Server 2028, which ships hardened by default with post-quantum key exchange
tldr: Windows Server 2028's public preview turns on hundreds of security settings from first boot, including Kerberos over NTLM and hybrid post-quantum TLS, and Microsoft warns that some older software may break.

title: A deployed four-city entanglement-based QKD network with real-time key delivery, benchmarked against finite-key security bounds
tldr: A Slovak quantum key distribution network links four cities over ordinary telecom fiber, runs all links at once and delivers finished keys to applications in real time, with honest post-processed key rates.
byline: Gilberto Borges, Saeid Salari, Ekta Panwar et al. · Institute of Physics, Slovak Academy of Sciences

title: Oracle patches Java4Shell, a Java runtime flaw that lets attackers take over widely used server software
tldr: Oracle fixed a memory-corruption flaw in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder that researchers used to run code on Jira, Confluence, Jenkins and Keycloak without logging in, and CISA urged immediate patching.

title: Apple says an internal update, not a cyberattack, knocked out iCloud sign-in, the App Store and other services
tldr: Apple's iCloud sign-in, App Store, Apple Music, iCloud Mail and school tools failed for hours on Tuesday; Apple blamed an internal update and its status page showed everything restored by 6 PM ET.

title: Japan's Fugaku supercomputer is taken offline after an intruder steals user details and login keys
tldr: RIKEN shut down Fugaku on November 14 after an intruder got into internal servers between November 10 and 13 and took details of 4,222 users plus stored login keys.

title: California bars Waymo's driverless cars from freeways, and the company halts freeway rides in every market
tldr: California's DMV called Waymo's driverless freeway driving an imminent hazard after robotaxis entered an active construction closure, and Waymo stopped freeway rides across all 15 of its US markets.

title: Exploited Before It Was Fixed? Vulnerability Timelines from Open, Machine-Readable Evidence
tldr: Public vulnerability records can show how long a flaw was exploited before a fix existed for only a small share of exploited vulnerabilities, because publishers rarely release patch and vendor dates.
byline: Cédric Bonhomme, Alexandre Dulaunoy · Computer Incident Response Center Luxembourg (CIRCL)

title: Attackers plant malware on CNN, BBC, Zoom and Salesforce pages through the web-testing service Optimizely
tldr: Attackers abused a flaw in Optimizely's signup flow to add malicious code to scripts that 178 organizations load on their websites, exposing visitors to theft of card details and cryptocurrency.

title: The US bars China from renting advanced chips in data centers in five countries and requires licenses for sales there
tldr: A new US Commerce Department rule restricts remote access to advanced chips housed in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, and makes large sales to those countries subject to licenses.

title: Italy's privacy regulator fines Meta €805 million because Facebook's Android app read users' photo galleries without specific consent
tldr: Italy's data protection authority fined Meta €805 million ($886 million) over a Facebook feature that scanned Android users' photos and videos to suggest posts, affecting about 20 million people.
byline: The Record, Sky TG24, Garante per la protezione dei dati personali

title: A software bug at JPMorganChase slows payments across US banks, with thousands of customers reporting problems
tldr: JPMorganChase blamed a software bug in its own on-premise systems for slow transactions on Monday that spread to customers of other banks and to Zelle transfers; it says there is no sign of a cyberattack.

title: An 11-year-old Linux kernel flaw called NoisyTCP lets remote attackers crash servers, and a patch is available
tldr: A flaw in the Linux kernel's TCP code, present for 11 years, lets unauthenticated attackers crash servers over the network; it cannot be used to run code, and a fix is out.

title: ULA's Vulcan rocket fails for the first time, destroying 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites
tldr: United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket failed about 10 minutes after liftoff on Sunday, losing 40 Amazon Leo satellites in the company's first total mission failure since it was formed in 2006.

title: SpaceX catches a Starship upper stage with its launch tower after nearly a day in orbit
tldr: SpaceX's Starship upper stage returned from orbit on Saturday and was caught by the arms of the launch tower it had left 22 and a half hours earlier, on the first attempt.

title: Attackers break into unpatched Check Point gateways through PHP2Shell and wipe servers at some Israeli organizations
tldr: Check Point says an attacker used the PHP2Shell flaws and a new privilege-escalation bug to take over unpatched Security Gateways, then wiped VMware ESXi servers at some Israeli organizations.

title: A failure in aging air traffic telecom equipment grounds every US departure for more than four hours
tldr: The FAA halted all US departures on Friday after legacy telecom switches and routers in the air traffic network started passing inconsistent data; officials linked the failure to patches made during an upgrade.

title: Trezor confirms spy implants in three Safe 5 hardware wallets sold by a Southeast Asian reseller
tldr: Trezor found extra circuit boards in three Safe 5 wallets bought from reseller CryptoBilis that capture recovery phrases from the screen and send them out over a cellular network; new firmware blocks them.

title: Starship reaches orbit and deploys 26 Starlink satellites, but its booster diverts into the Gulf instead of a tower catch
tldr: SpaceX's 15th Starship flight put 26 Starlink V3 satellites into orbit, but the Super Heavy booster was diverted into the Gulf and exploded; a first attempt to catch the upper stage could come Saturday.

title: Lessons Not Learned: Why Cross-Chain Bridges Keep Losing Billions the Same Way
tldr: Most cross-chain bridge losses since 2023 came from how bridges were set up, not from code bugs; a rubric scored from on-chain data, plus rate limits and emergency stops, would have cut modeled losses 105-fold.
byline: Mohsen Ahmadvand, Piotr Dobaczewski, Camille Bouzerand · Monad Foundation

title: A Microsoft 365 outage tied to Exchange Online knocks out email, Teams and Copilot for more than 12 hours
tldr: Microsoft 365 services that depend on Exchange Online failed worldwide from Thursday afternoon, and Microsoft's fixes had not brought sustained recovery more than 12 hours later.

title: Apache patches a critical HTTP/2 flaw in its web server that could let attackers run code remotely
tldr: Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71 fixes a critical race condition in its HTTP/2 module that could let an unauthenticated attacker run code on servers that have HTTP/2 switched on.

title: Police in nine countries seize 235 servers behind the Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC malware
tldr: An Operation Endgame action coordinated by Europol took down 235 servers and 257 domains used by three malware families and found about 6.4 million stolen credentials.

title: Google opens pre-orders for its first Gemini smart glasses, made with Warby Parker, Gentle Monster and Samsung
tldr: Google's camera-equipped "intelligent eyewear," starting at $395, is up for pre-order ahead of a December 10 launch, with privacy limits such as a tamper-checked recording light.

title: A Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing Architecture with Globally Driven Atom Arrays
tldr: A design for neutral-atom quantum computers that picks which qubits to operate on by moving helper atoms, letting simple global laser and microwave pulses run error-corrected computation in simulation.
byline: Zhihao Zhang, Shuaifan Cao, Xinyang Yu et al. · Fudan University

title: Attackers push rogue remote-access clients to hundreds of PCs through managed service providers' ScreenConnect panels
tldr: Attackers used cloud-hosted ScreenConnect panels to install rogue remote-access software on at least 288 computers at 48 organizations; ConnectWise disabled five third-party extensions across about 400 partner environments.

title: Maersk confirms data theft from a legacy logistics system as a ransomware gang demands $5 million
tldr: Maersk says attackers stole data from an isolated system inherited through an acquisition; the WhiteArmor gang claims about 100GB and wants $5 million in bitcoin within 30 days.

title: The EU proposes a Digital Fairness Act to ban dark patterns, rein in addictive design and limit loot boxes for minors
tldr: The European Commission's draft Digital Fairness Act would ban manipulative "dark patterns," let users switch off addictive features, curb pay-to-win games for minors and allow fines of up to 6% of global turnover.

title: IBM's quantum roadmap swaps nine linked chips for two larger ones, targeting about 1,040 qubits in 2027
tldr: At its developer conference, IBM said its current Nighthawk r2 chip runs circuits of over 7,500 operations, and planned a 520-qubit Nighthawk r3 for 2027, with two chips linked into a roughly 1,040-qubit system.

title: Machine-learning decoders for fusion-based quantum computing in real time
tldr: PRISM, a transformer-based decoder for photonic quantum computers, matches slower integer-programming decoders on accuracy and runs on an AMD FPGA with 6.59-microsecond latency.
byline: Daniel Barter, Jacob C. Bridgeman, Chris Dawson et al.

title: France formally blames Iran's Revolutionary Guards for the cyberattacks that heated supermarket freezers
tldr: France says an Iranian Revolutionary Guards cyber unit sabotaged refrigeration controllers at more than 700 grocery stores, causing at least 15 fires, and plans to push for EU sanctions.

title: Microsoft's November Patch Tuesday fixes over 1,000 flaws, including an Outlook bug already used to steal logins
tldr: Microsoft's monthly updates fix between 1,093 and 1,235 vulnerabilities depending on how they are counted, including an exploited Outlook spoofing flaw, alongside patches from Apple, Google, Mozilla and Adobe.

title: N-able takes its N-central remote-management cloud offline after a researcher publishes 30-plus unpatched flaws
tldr: After a researcher released working exploits for more than 30 alleged flaws without warning, N-able shut down hosted N-central worldwide and told on-premises customers to switch their servers off.

title: Mitsui Chemicals agrees to buy photoresist maker JSR for $11.6 billion
tldr: Mitsui Chemicals will pay 1.84 trillion yen for JSR, a leading maker of the light-sensitive coatings used to print chip circuits, in the largest deal ever in Japan's chemicals sector.

title: SFU-Sim: Bit-Exact Reverse Engineering of NVIDIA MUFU and Validation of PTX Paths
tldr: SFU-Sim reverse-engineers how Nvidia GPUs compute sine, cosine and other special functions, and its model matches real hardware bit for bit on every input across three GPU generations.
byline: Haozhi Xie, Tao Su · Sun Yat-sen University

title: Attackers are exploiting the "SSHole" OpenSSH flaw on Alpine-style Linux servers days after the fix
tldr: Several security firms report real attacks on the OpenSSH and musl flaw CVE-2026-123158, which can give logins to passwordless accounts; OpenSSH 10.6p2 fixes it.

title: Vanderbilt University tells campus to shut down devices as the new BYOD ransomware gang claims an attack
tldr: Vanderbilt confirmed an active cyber incident and asked everyone to power off devices; a ransomware group called BYOD claims it stole data on over a million people.

title: Congress summons Nvidia's CEO over a reported Chinese spy operation, and Nvidia's board opens an investigation
tldr: House committee chairs asked Jensen Huang to brief them on November 18 about reported Chinese spying aimed at him; on Sunday Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation.

title: SonicWall patches a firewall VPN flaw that can sidestep SAML multi-factor login and is already exploited
tldr: SonicWall fixed seven SonicOS flaws, including CVE-2026-19868, which can bypass SAML-enforced MFA on SSL-VPN logins and was added to CISA's catalog of exploited bugs.
byline: SonicWall advisory (as quoted by SecurityWeek), BleepingComputer, Help Net Security

title: Chainalysis says hackers obtained credentials and live tokens for all of its users
tldr: Chainalysis, whose tools trace cryptocurrency flows, now says names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for every user were exposed, widening an incident first described as limited.

title: DigiCert says a 16-month exposure of an internal system let an outsider read customer identity documents
tldr: DigiCert says a server migration left an internal archive reachable from the internet from February 2025, and an unauthorized account read some customer records in June and July 2026.

title: Fox completes its $22 billion acquisition of Roku, five months after announcing it
tldr: Fox closed its $22 billion purchase of Roku, which reaches more than 100 million households, far earlier than the first-half-2027 completion the companies had projected.

title: AST SpaceMobile plans its own medium-lift rocket, backed by a $1.3 billion Firefly engine deal
tldr: The direct-to-phone satellite company says it will build Blacklift, a 20-ton-class rocket, and has committed $1.3 billion to Firefly for engines, a license and engineering support.

title: FaultScope: A software package for fast error attribution in quantum error correction
tldr: FaultScope is an open-source simulator that estimates how much each noisy component contributes to logical errors in quantum error correction, at under 1% extra runtime in tests.
byline: Yuguo Shao, Zhenyu Chen, Ningfeng Wang et al. · Yau Mathematical Sciences Center, Tsinghua University; Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications; Department of Computer Science and Technology, Tsinghua University

title: OpenSSH patch fixes "*sshole", a ten-year-old login bypass on musl-based Linux systems
tldr: OpenSSH 10.6p2 fixes a flaw, present since 2016, that lets an oversized password log in to accounts meant to refuse passwords on musl-based Linux systems such as Alpine.

title: Blue Origin pushes the next New Glenn launch into January 2027 after May launchpad explosion
tldr: Blue Origin's CEO told staff the next New Glenn flight is now targeted for January 2027, after earlier hopes of launching before the end of this year.

title: FAA begins replacing floppy-disk-based air traffic displays with a digital system at more than 400 facilities
tldr: The FAA says it will replace 1980s display systems that run on floppy disks with the digital E-IDS platform, targeting 435 sites by the end of 2028.

title: Beyond Sensitive APIs: Detecting Access Control Flaws at Sensitive Callsites in Android Firmware
tldr: Callix, a tool that judges whether access checks are strong enough for a sensitive operation, found 819 vulnerable paths in pre-installed apps from ten Android vendors.
byline: Haotian Deng, Meng Hao, Hanxiao Chen et al. · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

title: Second wave of attacks on refrigeration controllers hits supermarkets across Europe
tldr: Remote tampering with refrigeration controllers raised temperatures in more than 115 stores in six European countries on November 2, and also reached a French blood-service supplier, following a larger French wave in October.

title: Zyxel patches a switch flaw that was exploited on nearly 1,000 devices after being mistaken for an older bug
tldr: Zyxel fixed CVE-2026-107441 in ten GS1900 switch models after attackers used it to compromise 996 devices; the bug had been misattributed to an earlier, already-patched flaw.

title: Suspected Russian hackers use patched iPhone and Android flaws in watering-hole attacks
tldr: Sekoia says a group it links to Russia's foreign intelligence service used websites to profile visitors and attack phones that had not installed existing security updates.

title: DreamHost confirms a two-month breach of its File Manager exposed FTP logins and webmail sessions
tldr: Web host DreamHost says an attacker exploited a flaw in its File Manager from August to October 23, stealing FTP/SFTP credentials and some webmail session data.

title: Marvell agrees to buy Lumentum for $115 billion in an all-stock deal
tldr: Chip designer Marvell will acquire optical component maker Lumentum in an all-stock deal valued at $115 billion including debt, expected to close in the first half of 2028.

title: Google and partners dismantle XCPE botnet built into 1.3 million Android TV boxes
tldr: Google's Threat Intelligence Group and partners disrupted XCPE, a backdoor that a Chinese manufacturer shipped in more than 1.3 million Android TV boxes to rent out owners' internet connections.
byline: Krebs on Security, Ars Technica, The Register

title: Binance says a fake job interview started its $6.3 billion theft
tldr: Binance's incident report says a multi-stage attack beginning with a fake recruiter and malware led to the October 29 theft of about $6.34 billion, which the FBI attributed to North Korea's TraderTraitor group.

title: Apple warns memory costs are unprecedented as they squeeze margins and Mac supply
tldr: On its earnings call, Apple said memory pricing is unprecedented, forecast a December-quarter gross margin of 45 to 46 percent and expects Mac and iPad supply constraints.
